_comment: Source of truth for the Design tab's table: the object-driven tool offer, its Speed Dial tiles and its
Every verb, the selections it accepts, the document state it needs, and its fixed
compass address. Extracted from the code, not from memory:
call sites at 524/662/734/790/874/904, sk_key table at 369-400, m_keys_feature)
Design commands            -> a verb's `tool` block, and the entries with no slot (commands only):
the silent form's access, params and examples; McpToolsCad.cpp binds each block to its function
gen_offer_table.py emits src/slic3r/GUI/CAD/DesignOffer.hpp from this file, so the map
exists once. Edit the atlas and regenerate; never hand-edit the header.

slots.label: Create
slots.why: makes new geometry from nothing you have yet

slots.label: Remove
slots.why: takes material away Shell lives here by decision of 2026-08-01, not by oversight.

slots.label: Fillet / chamfer / draft
slots.why: finishes faces and edges without changing the shape's intent; named for the tools it holds, not for the trade word. RATIFIED 2026-08-01: Shell stays in Remove and Delete Face in Modify — this row is deliberately NOT the same set as the toolbar's dressup dropdown, which groups all five. Shell hollows a solid, so it belongs with the verbs that take material away. Do not re-open: a verb's row is its address and reordering breaks learned reach.

slots.label: Modify
slots.why: edits or removes what is already there

slots.label: Top
slots.why: the verbs a selection is opened for most. A flat slot is not a family: its verbs sit first, at the top level of the offer, each an item of its own, and its label is never shown. Appended last, so no ratified index moved.

verbs.name: Sketch
verbs.refusal: Select a flat face or a reference plane to sketch on
verbs.hint: Sketch on the selected flat face or plane, or click one next

verbs.name: Extrude
verbs.refusal: Create a sketch, or pick a solid face, first
verbs.hint: Extrude a sketch profile, or push/pull a picked face

tool.summary: Extrude a committed sketch, one of its loops, a face or a drawn profile into a body.
tool.details: A committed sketch, or one loop of it, extrudes as the Extrude card does; push/pull grows a planar face of a body; a profile drawn here is an explicit closed `profile` (list of [x,y]) or a centred width x height rectangle on `plane`. End conditions match Onshape. Reply: extrude_index, the index of its sketch (-1 for a face), the boolean and body used, end, frame.

params.name: sketch
params.description: a committed Sketch feature to extrude (sketch_commit's sketch_index); profile, width, height and plane are then refused

params.name: loop
params.description: with sketch: one closed loop (closed_loops[].index of sketch_describe {sketch}) with the loops inside it as holes; a hole is a loop of its own, so its index extrudes the disc. Omit for the whole sketch

params.name: face
params.description: push/pull: a planar face (query_topology id) of `body` grown along its outward normal (flip for inward); boolean auto joins that body. sketch, loop, profile, width, height, plane and taper are then refused, and end is blind or symmetric

params.name: plane
params.description: "XY", "XZ" or "YZ" through modeling_origin; {"datum": i}, a Plane feature; or {"body": b, "face": f}, a planar face (origin at its centroid, normal out of the body, x from the world axes). The reply's frame gives the axes.

params.name: profile
params.description: optional closed contour [[x,y],...] in plane mm; overrides width/height

params.name: boolean
params.description: auto joins the body the profile touches, else makes a new body, as the card's default; default auto with sketch, new without

params.name: body
params.description: the body to join, subtract from or intersect, or whose face is pushed; omit for the body a sketch touches, else the last body

params.name: distance2
params.description: second-side depth when end=two_sided (else falls back to distance)

params.name: up_to_face
params.description: face id (query_topology) of the body the extrude works on, when end=up_to_face

params.name: taper
params.description: draft/taper of the side wall

Reply: revolve_index, the index of its sketch, the boolean, body and axis used, frame.

verbs.name: Thicken Surface
verbs.refusal: Thicken Surface needs a surface body — make one with a Surface tool first
verbs.hint: Thicken a sheet body into a solid

tool.summary: Thicken a whole sheet body into a solid.
tool.details: A sheet of several faces whose free rims close into planar loops (the walls of a box with no lids) is capped at them and grows inward, into the closed shape that makes, whatever flip says; one whose rim can't be capped is refused. A single face or a closed shell is offset face by face along each face's normal, the one query_topology gives, or against it with flip; a closed shell can fail to thicken this way.

verbs.hint: Drill a hole, centered on a picked face or placed on a plane

tool.details: Reply: hole_index, body, x and y in the frame, off_plane with at, frame.

params.name: x

params.name: y

verbs.name: Thread
verbs.refusal: Pick a cylindrical surface (bore / outer) or a circular edge for a thread
verbs.hint: Thread a cylindrical surface (inner bore / outer) or a circular edge

tool.summary: Cut a thread as the Thread card does, along a cylindrical face or a circular edge, or on a plane.
tool.details: On a face a bore is tapped, a boss threaded; on a plane the thread goes at (x,y) or `at`. Without designation, a face or edge takes the nearest standard size, ISO metric and UTS alike. Long threads take seconds and the reply may be a job. Reply: thread_index, designation (null when custom), internal, diameter, pitch, depth, length, body, x, y, frame.

params.name: face
params.description: a cylindrical face id of `body` (query_topology); the thread runs its length from its lower end

params.name: edge
params.description: instead of face: a circular edge id of `body`, the thread rising along its normal; needs length

params.name: body
params.description: the body of face or edge, or the body threaded on a plane; omit for the last body (on a plane, a face plane's body)

params.name: designation
params.description: e.g. M5, M8x1, 1/4-20 UNC: sets diameter, pitch and depth

params.name: internal
params.description: true taps a hole, false threads a rod; required on a plane, else from the face (a bore is internal), external for an edge

params.name: diameter
params.description: nominal (major) diameter, replacing the standard's; with pitch, a custom thread

params.name: pitch
params.description: replaces the standard's

params.name: depth
params.description: radial depth; default the 60 degree V's for the pitch and role

params.name: length
params.description: default the face's length; required for an edge or a plane

params.name: plane
params.description: "XY", "XZ" or "YZ" through modeling_origin; {"datum": i}, a Plane feature; or {"body": b, "face": f}, a planar face to drill into that body (origin at its centroid, normal into the body, x along its longest edge). The reply's frame gives the axes.

params.name: x
params.description: on a plane: offset in the plane's frame from its origin, NOT world

params.name: y
params.description: on a plane: offset in the plane's frame from its origin, NOT world

params.name: at
params.description: on a plane, instead of x and y: a world point [x, y, z], or {"body": b, "face": f} a cylindrical face or {"body": b, "edge": e} a circular edge whose axis the thread shares, as hole takes it

tool.summary: Trim or extend the open sketch's entity nearest `at`, as a Trim or Extend click there does.
tool.details: Trim: a line or an arc is cut back from its end nearer `at` to the first crossing with another entity beyond `at`; a circle loses the part between the crossings either side of `at` and becomes an arc. With extend, as an Extend click: the line's or arc's end nearer `at` runs out to the next entity. The entity's constraints are released. Reply: entity, geometry (its new fields), released_constraints, entities, dof.

tool.summary: Move, rotate, scale or array entities of the open sketch, as the transform tools' Confirm does.
tool.details: move {dx, dy}, rotate {angle, pivot} and scale {scale, pivot} change the entities and release the constraints that no longer hold. array {dx, dy, count} adds copies stepped by dx, dy; polar_array {pivot, angle, count} adds copies every angle/count about pivot (angle is the whole sweep, default 360 degrees). count includes the original, and each copy is bound to its source (equal length and parallel, or its radius). pivot defaults to the entities' centroid. Angles are radians, or degrees as angle_deg. Reply: moved and released_constraints, or first_index, added and bound; pivot; entities, dof.

tool.summary: Add a constraint to the open sketch, as a CONSTRAIN bar button does (sketch_set_value is the value field, V).
tool.details: With `entities`, else the selection, the button's own rules choose the points, and a value it would ask for is `value` or the current one. With `refs` the references are taken as written, in sketch_constraints' form: {entity, role} for a point (role p0, p1 or center; entity also "origin") and {entity} for a whole entity (also "x_axis", "y_axis"). distance, lock_x, lock_y, point_on_line and point_on_object have no button and take refs. A constraint the sketch cannot solve with is rolled back and the call fails. Reply: added (indices), items, constraints, dof, solve_ok.
